catalog: In this course, students will explore the Internet of Things using a combination of lecture and laboratory practice. Topics include, but are not limited to, IoT Architectures, Sensors and Microcontrollers, Synthetic Sensors, Digital and Analog Electronics, Python and C programming for IoT, Sampling Strategies, Connectivity and Networks, Data Analysis and Data Management. In the laboratory component, students will design and build IoT solutions according to design requirements provided by the instructor.

goals.detail: the architectures and devices which comprise Internet of Things systems.
the structural alignment between physical processing constraints and sensor data throughput in real-timme edge applications.
IoT systems by combining physical sensors, actuators, and microcontroller-integrated software and hardware components.
edge devices to collect, serialize, and transmit operational data across a local network to coordinate system behavior.
IoT system architectures, distinguishing between edge node operations and a central hub.
collaborative, network IoT system design requirements through physical testing.

assess.name: Lab reports
assess.description: Handwritten, live report of what was accomplished during lab.

assess.name: Lab practical 1
assess.description: Lab practical of physical system, graded according to live performance of task. For this practical, students will need to setup a physical prototype from scratch on their own, and write/run MicroPython code that successfully publishes to a central MQTT broker.

assess.name: Lab practical 2
assess.description: Lab practical of physical system, graded according to live performance of task. For this practical, students will need to setup a physical prototype from scratch on their own, and write/run MicroPython code that successfully publishes to a central MQTT broker AND successfully subscribes to a particular Edge node and receives a custom message.

assess.name: Lab practical 3
assess.description: Lab practical of physical system, graded according to live performance of task. For this practical, each student will bring in an edge device that they have pre-built and pre-programmed to act as a member of a class-wide team in completing a pre-announced scenario mission.

assess.name: Exam 1
assess.description: In class, sit-down, paper exam. No notes or resources outside of a pencil and eraser. Covers the first module of the course.

assess.name: Exam 2
assess.description: In class, sit-down, paper exam. No notes or resources outside of a pencil and eraser. Covers the first and second module of the course.

assess.name: Exam 3
assess.description: In class, sit-down, paper exam. No notes or resources outside of a pencil and eraser. Covers all three modules of the course.

assess.name: Quizzes
assess.description: A short in-class quiz each week on the prior week's reading and concepts.
